parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the std-only Rust 2021 conversion, root test15.rs entry, exact CLI defaults, same output, and black-box reference probing obligations.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and verification but also spawned a probe_reference child; the child independently implemented a second /output project instead of returning only probe findings.
parallel.implementation: The parent built args/app/hopscotch_map modules with C++-style prefix integer parsing, while the child later wrote a different test15/lib/cli/hopscotch_map implementation into the same output paths.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact was a mixed tree containing parent app.rs and args.rs plus child cli.rs and child-sized entry/lib files; official artifact validation still accepted the package.
parallel.verification: The parent ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc, and reference comparisons before the child overwrite; the child separately built and checked normal cases after overwriting.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed 40/40, but the parent did not re-verify the final mixed tree after the child changed the deliverable and then interrupted the child before a clean returned handoff.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the required Rust project, root test15.rs, std-only implementation, default and --a argument behavior, and same stdout format.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, build, verification, and final response, with no delegated work or shared ownership boundary.
serial.implementation: It wrote Cargo.toml, test15.rs, cli.rs, hopscotch_map.rs, program.rs, and lib.rs, using HashMap-style unique lookup and direct Rust parse-based integer handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial final artifact was one coherent project tree with one entry point and one module set; there was no competing writer or mixed implementation provenance.
serial.verification: It built with Cargo and rustc, checked documented normal outputs, ignored extra args, negative count, and malformed/out-of-range abort cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed 40/40, but the serial code did not model C++ std::stoi prefix acceptance for values like 12abc, an ordinary implementation gap not exposed by the official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, root test15.rs, exact CLI, output, and black-box probing requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same high-level requirements and produced the required Cargo project and root entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel probed and implemented prefix-style std::stoi behavior, while serial used stricter Rust integer parsing and therefore missed that edge case despite passing official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned the main solution while a probe child ran concurrently, but the child also took implementation ownership in /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all probing, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery under one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping ownership of the deliverable workspace; serial had a single coherent owner and no competing implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child brief content is encrypted, but the observable child action used the same /output interface as the parent and produced separate source files rather than a returned probe-only handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface and no handoff; the same actor used its own discovered behavior to write and test the project.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's interface boundary was a shared output tree with ambiguous ownership; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote args/app/hopscotch_map modules and the child later wrote a different cli/lib/hopscotch_map entry path; both implementations matched official cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one implementation using cli/program/hopscotch_map modules and a direct parse-based CLI path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ended with a hybrid of two implementation paths, whereas serial stayed internally coherent but less faithful on std::stoi prefix parsing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on the child several times, interrupted it, resumed it, and interrupted it again without a clean completed child result being returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all findings and verification stayed in the single trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's child lifecycle created stale and partial child work in the workspace, while serial had no retrieval or handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent verified one project, then the child wrote another entry path and package metadata into /output; the later listing and artifact show a mixed submitted tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact contains only one project layout and no concurrent writer artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered a deliverable overwrite and mixed provenance; serial delivered one uninterrupted final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent ran cargo test, release build, rustc, and reference comparisons before the child changed the final tree; the child separately built and checked normal cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built with Cargo and rustc, then checked normal outputs and abort cases from the same implementation it delivered.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was split across actors and stale relative to the final mixed artifact; serial verification corresponded to its single delivered tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent extra time and tokens on a child that timed out under waits, was interrupted, resumed, and was interrupted again after changing the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in a shorter single-agent path with no child waits, interruptions, or shared-state cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had redundant coordination overhead but still closed successfully; serial was simpler and faster while also passing official tests.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current official cell/status.json evaluations are completed passes at 40/40, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The material process difference is that serial solved in one coherent path, while parallel solved with redundant child work and an adverse child overwrite of the deliverable after parent verification. The official evaluator still accepted the final parallel artifact.
parallel_contributors: Parent and child each produced a working project path; the final child-overwritten entry path still passed official tests.
Parallel probed std::stoi prefix behavior and its final child/parent implementations modeled that behavior more closely than serial.
serial_contributors: Serial maintained one implementation and verification pipeline with no shared-workspace collision.
Serial passed the official suite despite a stricter parse::<i32>() edge-case gap.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial did not implement C++ std::stoi numeric-prefix acceptance for inputs such as 12abc, which is an ordinary implementation difference rather than a parallel coordination error.
evaluator_effects: The official 40-case evaluator did not distinguish the serial parse-prefix gap because serial still received 40/40.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation with no official outcome difference

candidates.reason: Implementation had active owners in both the parent and child; the issue was overlapping writes, not absence of an implementer.
The parent integrated and verified its own project, and the final issue was a concrete later overwrite rather than nobody owning reconciliation.
A root test15.rs, Cargo project, and executable were assembled; the retained problem is the later child replacement of that deliverable.
The parent owned an end-to-end implementation, build, test, and final response pipeline even though a child later interfered with the tree.
Reference probing occurred before implementation, but it did not block all productive work behind a mandatory serial gate with unfinished consequences.
The run did not complete all investigation as a separate first phase that left later implementation incomplete or insufficiently verified.
No indispensable implementation or correction path was starved; the parent completed and verified a candidate before the child overwrite.
There was one child and no collective fan-out or retry breadth exhausting the official time or token budget before closure.
The child did not merely receive an overbroad unfinished scope; it wrote and built a project, and the adverse event is the concrete deliverable overwrite.
The child's exact encrypted brief cannot prove a known requirement was omitted, and the child implemented the visible task behavior rather than producing unusable work from a missing requirement.
A missing interface contract is not directly visible because the brief is encrypted; the observable event is the later concrete overwrite of the entry deliverable.
There is no observed known finding that disappeared during transfer and caused repeated work; the child independently worked in the shared output tree.
No large completed handoff reached the parent and remained unconsumed; the child did not return a bulky result before being interrupted.
The parent did not consume a stale child report describing superseded workspace state; the problem happened through direct writes.
No incompatible reports were returned and left unadjudicated at a parent decision point; the conflict was materialized as file replacement.
Although the parent verification became stale, there is no parent-visible unresolved integrated mismatch cited before closure; the direct boundary is the child deliverable overwrite.
No replacement child retried the task without inherited checkpoints; the same child was interrupted and later resumed rather than a checkpoint-free retry.

The child did not complete a retrievable implementation handoff that the parent ignored; it directly wrote into the shared output tree.
The child was not a verifier returning a concrete finding trapped below the parent; no unreturned verifier result is visible.
The child was interrupted rather than failing a required scope, and the parent already had a complete passing implementation path.
